summary: NDR feed s075_single is degraded: 25.7% of frames (839/3264) remain VXLAN-encapsulated (VNI 839) exceeding 10% threshold, hiding inner traffic from inspection. All other checks (duplicates, one-way, VLANs, truncation, drops, overload, encryption, oversize) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding VXLAN-encapsulated traffic without decapsulation. 839 of 3264 frames (25.7%) still carry VXLAN header (VNI 839), indicating tunnel termination/stripping is not configured on the visibility fabric before delivery to the tool.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR sees only outer VXLAN/IP/UDP headers for ~26% of traffic and cannot inspect inner Ethernet/IP/ports/payload. With needs_full_payload=true and needs_both_directions=true, this blinds detection, breaks flow correlation, and reduces coverage for overlay/lateral-movement traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Stripping VXLAN at the packet broker exposes inner L2-L7 headers and payload to the NDR, restoring full-payload inspection without requiring the NDR to decode tunnels itself.
